newsitem.title: USA: ADR REPORT - Copel launch well received.
newsitem.headline: ADR REPORT - Copel launch well received.

text.p: Brazilian state-owned electric company Companhia Paranaense de Energia (Copel) saw its American Depositary Shares (ADS) become the third most active stock on the New York Stock Exchange during its first day of trading Wednesday, dealers said.
"It's a hot deal," said one trader, adding that the offer was oversubscribed. "It's a high-growth area. There's a lot of untapped market down there, tied with a fairly solid company."
At midday Copel shares were trading at 19, a full point above their opening price.
Copel launched its Level Three ADS as part of a combined local and foreign offering of Preferred B shares to raise money for its 1997 and 1998 investment programs.
Dresdner Kleinwort Benson and Lehman Brothers were the joint global coordinators and bookrunners of the launch.
One dealer said the launch of an ADR or ADS was usually very active during the first few days of trading. (There is no technical difference between an ADS and an ADR.)
"It's normal," he said, adding that trading in Copel would likely settle down once the euphoria had subsided.
Brazil's telephone holding company Telebras SA was up 1-3/8 at 152-5/8 following a market rise in Brazil on news of Gustavo Franco's nomination as the new central bank chief.
"The market likes him," said a dealer. Franco is the former international affairs director of the central bank.
Among European ADRs, Royal Dutch Petroleum Co was up 8/16 at 55-9/16 a day after news about its plans to enter Japan's competitive gasoline retail market.

Akzo Nobel NV was one point lower at 72-1/2 amid apparent investor worry that its earnings -- to be released Thursday -- might not be as good as expected. Concern arose after Dutch chemical group DSM NV reported earnings at the lower end of expectations.
Creative Technology Ltd was down 1-5/16 at 20-1/4, Saville System Plc was up 6-1/4 at 63, while Telefonos de Mexico was up 1-1/2 at 54-1/8.
Advancers led decliners 295 to 198 among 814 ADRs. The ADR group was up 0.73 percent on volume of 47.9 million ADRs.
